tasks.short: Keep hazardous inventories and judge how materials are handled.

steps.what: Count hazardous materials and wastes on the store shelves.
Decide whether those materials are handled properly.
Fill waste tracking row v1 for these inventories in the waste tracking system.
Check the inventories row in the waste tracking system still matches the counted materials.
Tell the warehouse clerk which materials are not handled properly.

tasks.design: She counts the lots and decides whether they are handled properly. A separate step files waste tracking row v1 in the waste tracking system ({OTHER}) from those counts only, and she checks that version before it stands. The filing does not raise an alert, does not send a transfer note, and does not report to the inspectorate; she tells the warehouse clerk herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts sat in a notebook and were typed again into the waste tracking system, where a column was easy to miss.
tasks.enabler_now: A records screen can file a row from fields she has already named on the walk.
tasks.still_hard: A lot with no label, or a quantity that will not fit a field, still needs her eyes and a handwritten row.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a drum is in the wrong cupboard even when the quantity matches.
tasks.altitude: She still counts the store, judges handling, checks every filed row and tells the clerk. She stops retyping a count she has already named. She does not gain a right to let a list judge a hazard or to send a note out.

reach.task: Record a hazardous lot as it arrives
reach.learn: Which of substance, location, quantity, unit, date and waste code are already on the delivery note.

evidence.claim: Arbo rules and systems that can monitor behaviour or performance need works-council consent. This row does not record who handled a lot.
Serious accidents must be reported at once to the Labour Inspectorate. This inventory filing does not make that report.
Monitoring or evaluating workers' behaviour is high-risk. This inventory row does not score staff.
Model knowledge, not a measured study of this store: only the retype of a count she has already named can disappear. The walk, the judgement and the talk with the clerk stay.

assumptions: On the walk she names substance, location, quantity, unit, received date and waste code. That capture sits in the count step and is not saved.
The warehouse clerk keeps the column names outside this task. If she will not name a quantity, or a column is missing, the filing step does not run and she writes the row by hand.
The row does not store an employee name, a sickness cause, or a score. Telling the clerk is spoken in the room. It is not a message, not a send, and not a second commit.
The filing step does not read a safety data sheet, does not raise an alert, does not send a transfer note, and does not report an accident.
A later edit voids the check of waste tracking row v1. Her reading of that version is the check step, already inside the task, and is not deducted again.
Upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 hours of this task is her time telling the clerk that a column will not take a quantity, then writing that row by hand.
unknowns: Whether this company's waste tracking row is the legal hazardous-waste register.
Whether the works council has already consented to the waste tracking system.
research_questions: Which of substance, location, quantity, unit, date and waste code does the warehouse clerk already record before she walks the store?

incremental.description: When a column is missing or she will not name a quantity, tell the clerk and write that inventory row by hand.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a month of unlabelled lots, so she writes every row by hand. High is 4, the retype only, and only when she has already named substance, location, quantity, unit, date and waste code. The walk, the handling judgement and the talk with the clerk stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect samples for disease, purity and cleanliness.

steps.what: List the stored laboratory method for these samples.
Perform physical inspections of the samples in the lab.
Decide whether samples fail purity or show disease.
Fill lab result v1 with the analyses she named.
Check the result still records these laboratory analyses.
Tell the site manager whether samples fail cleanliness.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} lists the stored method card, then she inspects the sample and decides the finding herself. A separate step files lab result v1 in the {DOCS} with that finding only, and she checks that version before it stands. The filing does not raise an alert, does not send the result, and does not judge the hazard; she tells the site manager herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The method lived in a binder and the finding was written again into the log.
tasks.enabler_now: A stored method card can be listed, and a finding she has already named can be filed into fixed fields.
tasks.still_hard: Looking at the sample, and judging disease, purity or cleanliness, cannot be skipped.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a smell or a film the method card does not name.
tasks.altitude: She still inspects every sample, judges the finding, checks the filed result and tells the site manager. She stops hunting a method card and retyping a finding she has already named. She does not gain a right to let a list call a hazard or to send the result out.

reach.task: Keep the record of why an employee is sick
reach.learn: Whether a sample line would name a worker's illness. It must not.

evidence.claim: In LabSafety Bench no model passed 70% accuracy at hazard identification. This design does not ask a model to judge the sample.
A Dutch authority fined a maintenance firm for recording why employees were sick; that belongs with the company doctor. This lab result does not store a worker's illness.
Model knowledge, not a measured study of these inspections: only the retype of a finding she has already named can disappear. The inspection, the judgement and the talk with the site manager stay.

assumptions: The lab lead keeps, outside this task, method name, what to look for, and the pass limit. If that card is blank, the list returns nothing and she inspects from the paper method at full time.

In the decision step she names sample id, pass or fail, and one short observation. That capture is counted there. If the observation will not fit one line, or a result field is missing, the filing step does not run and she writes the log by hand.
The result stores the sample, the method and her finding. It does not store an employee's name or why someone is sick. No recording is made.
The filing step does not judge the hazard, does not raise an alert, and does not send the result to the site manager, a customer, or an inspectorate. She speaks the finding herself.
A later edit voids the check of lab result v1. Her reading of that version is the check step, already inside the task, and is not deducted again.
Upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 hours of this task is writing the log by hand when the method card is blank or the finding will not fit a field.
unknowns: Whether a workplace swab or sample result is kept as a medical record.
Which methods the lab lead has already written as a method card.
research_questions: For a routine sample, are method name, what to look for, and the pass limit already stored before she opens the binder?

incremental.description: When the method card is blank or the finding will not fit one line, write the lab result by hand.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a week of odd samples where the method card is blank and she writes the log by hand. High is 2, the retype of a finding she has already decided, and only when the method card and the result fields are present. The inspection, the judgement and the talk with the site manager stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still counts the store, judges handling, inspects each sample, checks every filed version and tells her colleagues in person. She stops retyping a count or a finding she has already named. She does not gain a right to let a list judge a hazard, file a version she has not read, or send a note outside the company.
reach: warehouse clerk (which hazardous lots arrived, with substance, quantity and waste code)
company doctor (whether a sample line would name an employee's illness)
skills_to_grow: Write the inventory row by hand when a quantity will not fit a field.
Inspect from the paper method when the method card is blank.
Refuse a lab line that would store why an employee is sick.
role.ambitious_version: Each lot already has a complete row before she finishes the walk, and each sample has a method card before she opens the bench. She still decides whether the lot is handled properly and whether the sample fails. The filed version is not sent out, and she still tells the clerk and the site manager herself.
